args.message: fix: use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

args.body:
## Summary
`round_money` in `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, but FIN-212 requires banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`) to the nearest cent. This caused the nightly build failure in `tests/test_money.py` (e.g. `Decimal("2.665")` rounded to `2.67` instead of `2.66`).

## Change
- Switch the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

## Testing
- CI run `ci-0001` passed on commit `08d3cd5986` (includes `tests/test_money.py`).

transcript.reasoning_content:
Wait, the test says 2.675 -> 2.68 under ROUND_HALF_EVEN? 2.675: 7 is odd... half-even rounds to even last digit: 2.67 (7 odd → round to 8? half-even rounds to even digit, so 2.68 since 8 is even). Hmm, 2.675 halfway between 2.67 and 2.68; even digit is 8, so 2.68. Correct. 2.665: halfway between 2.66 and 2.67; 6 is even → 2.66. So ROUND_HALF_EVEN passes both tests. Also note quantize with Decimal("2.675") is exact since Decimal is base-10. Fix: change ROUND_HALF_UP to ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

Note: 2.675 under ROUND_HALF_UP would also give 2.68, so the distinguishing test is 2.665 (HALF_UP would give 2.67).

Create branch, commit, run CI.
